newsitem.title: UK: Life-saving explorers to receive UK rescue honour.
newsitem.headline: Life-saving explorers to receive UK rescue honour.

text.p: Two arctic explorers who risked their lives to save a fellow adventurer on the polar ice cap are to receive Britain's highest rescue honour, the Royal Humane Society said on Tuesday.

Briton David Hempleman-Adams and Norwegian Rune Gjeldnes battled temperatures of minus 70 degrees Celsius to clear a landing strip on unstable ice so a plane could evacuate a lone traveller who had fallen into the frozen waters.
They will receive the Royal Humane Society Medal, the society said.

British explorer Alan Bywaters had been attempting to reach the North Pole when he broke through the ice and lost all his equipment. He managed to climb back on to the ice and follow the tracks of the other team, arriving with severe hypothermia and frostbite.
Hempleman-Adams and Gjeldnes administered first aid, radioed for help and then fought for 12 hours to clear a landing strip for a plane to land.

"This was an extremely hazardous rescue in conditions which the bulk of us cannot even imagine. Without the efforts of Hempleman-Adams and Gjeldnes, Bywaters would almost certainly have died," the secretary of the Humane Society said in a statement.
After using vital equipment and food in a 12-hour rescue effort, the pair were forced to abandon their expedition.
